KEY MESSAGE 1...Periodic showers and thunderstorms are expected through
Thursday. Some storms may be severe through this early evening
and especially on Wednesday into Wednesday night.

Aloft, W'erly to WNW'erly 500 mb flow near 40 to 50 knots and
embedded mid/upper-level shortwave troughs affect Western and 
Central NY through Thursday. At the surface, a synoptic front, 
augmented by Lake Erie and Lake Ontario lake breezes, will 
remain nearly-stationary between the southern shore of Lake 
Ontario and the northern shore of Lake Erie in/near our forecast
area through this early evening. The front is then expected to 
drift N'ward and across Lake Ontario later this evening through
early Wednesday afternoon as a low wobbles E'ward across 
northern ON to near James Bay. An especially-humid air mass 
originating over the Gulf will reside in the warm sector, 
generally south of the front. Our entire CWA is then expected to
reside in the warm and very humid sector the rest of Wednesday 
before a cold front sweeps SE'ward through our region during the
daylight hours of Thursday as the aforementioned low wobbles 
farther E'ward across northern QC. Note: Note: periods of heavy 
rainfall are possible ahead of the cold front, amidst unusually-
high PWAT values, through Thursday (see details farther below).

Daytime highs should reach mainly the mid 70's to mid 80's today
and Wednesday, and mainly the lower 70's to lower 80's on
Thursday as a cooler air mass overspreads our region behind the
cold front. The aforementioned high humidity ahead of and
especially behind the first above-mentioned front will
contribute to limited nocturnal cooling tonight and Wednesday
night. Lows are expected to reach mainly the 60's to near 70F
around daybreak Wednesday and Thursday, respectively.

Mainly fair weather is expected for the time being. Isolated 
showers and thunderstorms remain possible through this early 
evening along the synoptic front in vicinity of I-90 in Western 
and Central NY. Rather dry mid-level air/resulting detrimental 
entrainment of unsaturated ambient air and stabilizing 
subsidence in the wake of a recent shortwave trough axis passage
will limit the potential for this convection to initiate. If 
showers and storms do develop, a few severe storms with 
damaging straight-line wind gusts are possible amidst moderate 
boundary layer CAPE, moderate to strong deep-layer bulk shear, 
and steep low-level lapse rates/moderate DCAPE. Any showers/storms
are expected to dissipate by mid-evening, in response to 
boundary layer stabilization via nocturnal cooling.

After midnight tonight and through daybreak Wednesday, isolated
to scattered showers and thunderstorms are possible as far east
as roughly the Genesee Valley in our CWA, in response to moist
isentropic ascent ahead of a shortwave trough axis and low-level
convergence/moist ascent along an attendant surface trough axis
releasing weak to moderate CAPE, including elevated CAPE, amidst
moderate to strong effective bulk shear. Can't totally rule-out
a severe storm with damaging straight-line wind gusts since
modest nocturnal cooling should allow DCAPE to remain sizable
and prevent DCIN from being excessive. Additional rounds of
organized showers and thunderstorms are expected the rest of 
Wednesday morning through Thursday, as deep-layer bulk shear 
remains moderate to strong and at least weak to moderate CAPE, 
including elevated CAPE, is released by the following: moist 
isentropic ascent ahead of shortwave trough axes; low-level 
convergence/moist ascent along surface trough axes attendant to 
the shortwave troughs and along the warm and cold fronts; 
downshear outflow boundaries interacting favorably with ambient 
low-level vertical wind shear. The greatest coverage of showers 
and thunderstorms is expected Wednesday afternoon through early 
evening, when daytime heating in the warm/moist sector should 
yield moderate to strong boundary layer CAPE. This is when 
severe storms in the form of multicells, including bow echoes, 
and supercells, appear most-likely. Damaging straight-line wind
gusts and damaging hail up to golf ball-size are expected to be
the main severe convective WX hazards due to the expectation of
steep low-level lapse rates/large DCAPE and mid-level lapse 
rates near 7C/km contributing to sizable MUCAPE in the hail 
growth zone. A tornado or two is possible since low-level winds 
may veer and strengthen significantly with height, resulting in
sizable surface-based ESRH amidst favorably-low mixed layer 
LCL's. Localized flash flooding is possible where showers and 
storms manage to train, which should be the case along the warm 
front and any outflow boundaries oriented roughly west-to-east, 
which will be largely parallel to W'erly to WNW'erly mean mid-
level flow.
